name: The Christian's Victory in Christ
path: Angelology: The Doctrine of Spiritual Beings

objectives.text: Identify from Bible stories and verses that Jesus is stronger than Satan
Name the cross and the empty tomb as the places where Jesus defeated Satan, sin, and death
Retell God's promise in Genesis 3:15 that the woman's offspring would crush the serpent's head
Recite Romans 8:38-39 and list the things Paul says cannot separate believers from God's love in Christ
Describe how Jesus overcame Satan's temptations in the wilderness by answering with the Word of God
Explain what 1 John 3:8 means by Jesus destroying the works of the devil using examples from His earthly ministry
Explain from Hebrews 2:14-15 why the Son took on flesh and how His death freed His people from slavery to the fear of death
Trace the promise of the serpent crusher from Genesis 3:15 through its fulfillment in Christ and the promise of Romans 16:20
Explain from Scripture that believers receive victory as a gift won by Christ rather than achieve it by their own strength
Explain how the resurrection of Christ defeats death and removes its sting according to 1 Corinthians 15
Explain from Luke 10:17-20 why Jesus directed His disciples to rejoice that their names are written in heaven rather than in power over spirits
Explain how Christ as King restrains and conquers all His and His people's enemies using Psalm 110 and its New Testament use
Analyze the already and not yet of Satan's defeat by comparing his overthrow at the cross with his final destruction
Interpret Colossians 2:13-15 in context to show how cancelling the record of debt at the cross disarmed the powers
Explain from Romans 8 and Revelation 12 why Satan's accusations cannot bring condemnation on those justified in Christ
Construct a summary of Christ's victory over Satan, sin, and death across His humiliation and exaltation with supporting texts
Compare the theme of Christ's conquest of the powers with penal substitution and explain how the Reformed tradition holds them together
Evaluate fear-driven and triumphalist views of the spiritual realm against the teaching of Scripture
Defend from Scripture and the confessions the finality of Christ's victory and the certainty of Satan's final judgment
Synthesize the biblical storyline into a theological essay presenting the gospel as Christ's conquest that secures His people forever

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (Jesus stronger than Satan, the cross, Genesis 3:15, Romans 8:38-39, 1 John 3:8, already and not yet, Colossians 2:15, Christ's kingship, assurance against accusation, theology of victory, evaluating fear-driven and triumphalist views, defending finality, final synthesis). Merged the duplicate grade 3 summary into later objectives. Dropped the James 4:7 resisting objective as it belongs to the Demons and Spiritual Warfare sibling, and reframed the weakness comparison as victory received from Christ. Added the wilderness temptation, Hebrews 2:14-15 and fear of death, tracing the serpent-crusher promise, resurrection and death's sting, Luke 10:17-20, and comparing Christ's conquest with penal substitution. Anchored with Heidelberg Catechism Q1, Q34, Q45, Q52, Q56, Westminster Shorter Catechism Q26, and Westminster Confession 8.8 and 33.2 where they state the doctrine.
